title: F-1 Academic Student Visa
description: Nonimmigrant visa for full-time students enrolled in SEVP-certified academic programs at US colleges, universities, seminaries, conservatories, academic high schools, and other academic institutions.

title: M-1 Vocational Student Visa
description: Nonimmigrant visa for students enrolled in vocational or other recognized nonacademic programs at SEVP-certified institutions.

title: J-1 Exchange Visitor Visa
description: Nonimmigrant visa for participants in exchange programs designated by the U.S. Department of State. 16 BridgeUSA categories including students, research scholars, short-term scholars, trainees, teachers, camp counselors, au pairs, and interns.

title: Optional Practical Training (OPT)
description: Temporary employment authorization for F-1 students in a job directly related to their major area of study. Up to 12 months pre- or post-completion. Requires I-765 EAD.

title: STEM OPT Extension
description: 24-month extension of OPT for F-1 students who have earned STEM degrees from SEVP-certified programs. Employer must be E-Verify enrolled. Form I-983 training plan required. Total OPT: 36 months.

title: Curricular Practical Training (CPT)
description: Work authorization for F-1 students for employment that is an integral part of an established curriculum, including co-op programs, internships, and practicums. Must be authorized by DSO before starting.

title: H-1B Specialty Occupation Worker
description: Nonimmigrant work visa for specialty occupation roles requiring at least a bachelor's degree or equivalent in a specific specialty. Annual cap: 65,000 regular + 20,000 U.S. master's exemption. Lottery system when oversubscribed. Employer-sponsored.

title: H-4 Dependent of H-1B
description: Nonimmigrant visa for spouses and unmarried children under 21 of H-1B holders. H-4 EAD available if principal's I-140 is approved or principal is in 7th year+ H-1B extension. H-4 EAD auto-extension eliminated effective October 30, 2025.

title: L-1A Intracompany Transferee — Executive/Manager
description: Nonimmigrant visa for executives and managers transferred from a qualifying foreign affiliate, subsidiary, or parent to the US entity. Employee must have worked abroad for at least 1 year in the past 3 years. Initial period: 3 years (1 year for new offices); extensions: 2-year increments; max 7 years.

title: L-1B Intracompany Transferee — Specialized Knowledge
description: Nonimmigrant visa for employees with specialized knowledge of the petitioning company's products, services, research, equipment, techniques, management, or procedures. Initial period: 3 years (1 year for new offices); extensions: 2-year increments; max 5 years.

title: L-2 Dependent of L-1
description: Nonimmigrant visa for spouses and unmarried children under 21 of L-1 holders. As of November 2021, L-2 spouses have incident-to-status work authorization (I-94 serves as EAD); I-765 not required for L-2 spouses.

title: O-1A — Extraordinary Ability (Sciences/Education/Business/Athletics)
description: Nonimmigrant visa for individuals with extraordinary ability in sciences, education, business, or athletics. No annual cap. Employer or agent sponsor required. Evidentiary criteria: major awards OR 3 of 8 criteria (prizes, membership, press, judging, contributions, publications, critical role, salary).

title: O-1B — Extraordinary Achievement (Arts/Film/TV)
description: Nonimmigrant visa for individuals with extraordinary achievement in the arts, or extraordinary ability in the motion picture or television industry. Distinct evidentiary criteria from O-1A.

title: O-3 Dependent of O-1
description: Nonimmigrant visa for spouses and unmarried children under 21 of O-1 holders. O-3 holders may not work in the US.

title: E-1 Treaty Trader
description: Nonimmigrant visa for nationals of treaty countries engaged in substantial trade principally between the US and the treaty country. Nationality requirement: both the individual and the employing company must be nationals of the same treaty country.

title: E-2 Treaty Investor
description: Nonimmigrant visa for nationals of treaty countries investing a substantial amount of capital in a US enterprise. More countries have E-2 than E-1 treaties. No minimum investment threshold specified by statute, but must be substantial relative to cost of buying/starting the business.

title: TN — USMCA Professional
description: Nonimmigrant status for Canadian and Mexican professionals in one of the USMCA Appendix 1603.D.1 listed occupations (63 categories including engineers, accountants, scientists, lawyers, etc.). No annual cap, no lottery, no employer petition required. Admitted at POE. Periods of 3 years, renewable indefinitely.

title: E-3 — Australian Specialty Occupation Worker
description: Nonimmigrant work visa for Australian nationals in specialty occupations. Requires LCA like H-1B but has a separate annual cap of 10,500. Spouses of E-3 holders may apply for EAD. Available to Australian nationals only.

title: H-1B1 — Chile/Singapore Free Trade Specialty Occupation
description: Specialty occupation work status for Chilean and Singaporean nationals under free trade agreements. Annual cap: Chile 1,400 / Singapore 5,400 (separate from regular H-1B cap). No lottery. Spouses not eligible for EAD. Available at consular posts.

title: EB-1 First Preference Employment-Based Green Card
description: Three subcategories: EB-1A (extraordinary ability, self-petition), EB-1B (outstanding professors/researchers, employer required), EB-1C (multinational managers/executives, employer required). No PERM required. August 2026 priority dates: India Oct 15 2022; China Jul 1 2023; Philippines Current.
eb_backlog_note: India and China retrogressed; Philippines Current

title: EB-2 Second Preference Employment-Based Green Card
description: For workers with advanced degrees or exceptional ability. PERM required unless National Interest Waiver (NIW) obtained. August 2026 priority dates: India UNAVAILABLE (FY2026 quota exhausted); China Sep 1 2021; Philippines Current.
eb_backlog_note: India FY2026 Unavailable; China multi-year queue

title: EB-3 Third Preference Employment-Based Green Card
description: For skilled workers (2+ years training/experience), professionals (BS degree), and unskilled workers. PERM required. August 2026 priority dates (Skilled/Prof): India Jan 1 2014; China Jan 1 2022; Philippines Aug 1 2023. Philippines EB-3 retrogression risk noted in Aug 2026 Bulletin.
eb_backlog_note: India: decade+ queue; Philippines: retrogression risk

title: PERM Labor Certification
description: Program Electronic Review Management (PERM) is the process by which employers obtain a labor certification from the Department of Labor, attesting that no qualified US workers are available for the position. Required for most EB-2 and EB-3 green cards. Filed on ETA Form 9089.

title: Form I-140 — Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers
description: Petition filed by employer (or self, for EB-1A/EB-2 NIW) to classify the alien worker in an employment-based immigrant category. Approval of I-140 locks in priority date. Filing fee: $715 + Asylum Program Fee. Premium processing: $2,965 for 15 business day adjudication.

title: Form I-485 — Adjustment of Status
description: Application to register permanent residence (green card) filed by aliens already in the US when an immigrant visa number is immediately available. Filing fee: $1,440 (age 14+, paper) / $1,390 (online); $950 (under 14 with parent). Includes biometrics. Combo EAD/AP card issued while pending.

title: SEVIS — Student and Exchange Visitor Information System
description: DHS system tracking F-1, M-1, and J-1 students and exchange visitors. SEVIS I-901 fee must be paid before applying for a visa or entering the US. Fees: $350 for F-1/M-1; $220 for J-1 (Sponsored J programs may be exempt).

title: F-2 Dependent of F-1
description: Nonimmigrant visa for spouses and unmarried children under 21 of F-1 holders. F-2 spouses may NOT work in the US; may study part-time. F-2 children may attend K-12 public school full-time but may not attend full-time post-secondary programs. Separate I-20 required for each F-2 dependent.

title: J-2 Employment Authorization
description: J-2 spouses and minor children of J-1 exchange visitors may apply for employment authorization via Form I-765. Not automatic — application required. Income earned by J-2 may not be used to support the J-1. Authorization period: up to J-1 program end or 4 years, whichever is shorter. Regulatory basis: 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(5).

title: USCIS Filing Fee Schedule (G-1055, May 2026)
description: USCIS fee schedule effective per G-1055 edition 05/29/26. Key fees: I-129 $780 (standard) / $390 (small employer); I-140 $715; I-485 $1,440 (paper) / $1,390 (online); I-765 $520 (paper standalone) / $470 (online); I-539 $420 (paper) / $370 (online); I-907 (Premium Processing) $2,965 for I-129/I-140. Asylum Program Fee applies additionally to most employer petitions.

title: DOS Visa Bulletin — August 2026 (Final Action Dates)
description: Monthly DOS Visa Bulletin sets priority date cutoffs for employment-based (EB) and family-based categories. USCIS announced use of Final Action Dates chart for AOS in August 2026. August 2026 highlights: EB-1 India Oct 15 2022; EB-2 India UNAVAILABLE; EB-3 India Jan 1 2014; China EB-2 Sep 1 2021; Philippines EB-3 retrogression risk.

title: E-1/E-2 Treaty Country Status
description: E-1/E-2 treaty eligibility by top-20 nationality. E-1 & E-2: MX, DE, GB, FR, CA, JP, CO, SV, HN, GT. E-2 only: PH, KR. No treaty: IN, CN, BR, VN, CU, DO, HT. Nigeria uncertain. Australia: E-3 (separate category).

title: TPS — El Salvador
description: Temporary Protected Status for El Salvador nationals. Last confirmed designation extends through September 9, 2026 (FR 90 FR 5953, Jan 17 2025). Statutory renewal decision deadline (July 11 2026) reportedly missed by DHS with no Federal Register announcement as of August 11 2026. Status uncertain — practitioners expect auto-extension to March 2027 but no official confirmation.
